conventions.convention: Bounded BV data are Lebesgue almost-everywhere classes with TV(u) = sup over h > 0 of h⁻¹∫|u(x+h)−u(x)| dx. Global integrability is not required.
Cells are [jh,(j+1)h), j ∈ ℤ; time indices start at zero. Initialization uses cell averages, and the update subtracts λ times right flux minus left flux.
Flux monotonicity and coordinate Lipschitz bounds are required on the initial essential-range square I². The full invariant-interval CFL condition is λ(L₁+L₂) ≤ 1.
W interpolates affinely between Uⁿ and Uⁿ⁺¹ on each time slab; the piecewise-constant reconstruction uses Uⁿ on that slab.
Entropy levels range over every real k, including levels outside I; q_k(s) = sgn(s−k)(f(s)−f(k)), with sgn(0)=0.
The convergence theorem assumes ACω, additionally DC when u₀ ∈ L¹(ℝ), and a positive lower bound τ_m/h_m ≥ c_*. Its convergence conclusions are local.

load_bearing.statement: Under the full invariant-interval CFL bound, H is nondecreasing in each coordinate on I³ and preserves constants. Every state remains in I, ∑_j|U_{j+1}ⁿ−U_jⁿ| ≤ TV(u₀), and (h/τ)∑_j|U_jⁿ⁺¹−U_jⁿ| ≤ (L₁+L₂)TV(u₀).

For bounded BV data and vanishing meshes satisfying the full invariant-interval CFL bound, every subsequence has a further subsequence whose linear interpolants converge uniformly in time in L¹(K) on every bounded interval K to a continuous local-L¹ map u with u(0)=u₀ and values in I. The piecewise-constant reconstructions converge strongly to the same u in local space-time L¹.
For every j ∈ ℤ, n ≥ 0 and k ∈ ℝ, |U_jⁿ⁺¹−k|−|U_jⁿ−k|+λ(G_k(U_jⁿ,U_{j+1}ⁿ)−G_k(U_{j−1}ⁿ,U_jⁿ)) ≤ 0, where G_k(a,b)=F(a∨k,b∨k)−F(a∧k,b∧k), and G_k(s,s)=q_k(s) for s ∈ I.

Assume ACω, T>0, f ∈ C¹(ℝ), bounded BV initial data, a locally Lipschitz consistent flux monotone on I², vanishing meshes with (τ_m/h_m)(L₁+L₂) ≤ 1 and τ_m/h_m ≥ c_*>0, and additionally DC if u₀ ∈ L¹(ℝ). Then there is a unique bounded Kruzhkov entropy solution with datum u₀; W_m converges in C([0,T];L¹_loc(ℝ)) and the piecewise-constant reconstructions converge strongly in local space-time L¹.
